title: Hershey (HSY) Suffers a Larger Drop Than the General Market: Key Insights
author: Zacks.Com
description: Hershey stock fell 1.82% on September 29, 2026, underperforming the S&P 500's 0.17% loss. The stock has declined 6.7% over the past month, lagging the Consumer Staples sector. However, the company maintains a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) rating with positive earnings expectations, projecting 62.31% EPS growth for the upcoming quarter and 34.55% growth for the full fiscal year.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: While the stock experienced a notable daily decline of 1.82% and a 6.7% monthly drop, underperforming the broader market, this is offset by strong fundamental expectations including 62.31% projected EPS growth for the upcoming quarter and a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) rating. The neutral sentiment reflects the mixed short-term weakness against positive long-term earnings outlook.

title: Can Hershey's Innovation & Brand Investments Strengthen Demand?
author: Na
description: The Hershey Company is ramping up demand creation efforts in the second half of 2026 by increasing brand investment by 30% year-over-year and launching 30% more innovation items, including new Hershey's Creme Filled Bars and Reese's Pieces with Cookie. The company is also strengthening seasonal programs and core-item availability to engage consumers amid selective spending patterns.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: While Hershey is implementing positive strategic initiatives (increased brand investment, innovation, and seasonal programs), the stock has underperformed its industry over the past three months (down 6.3% vs. industry down 5.7%), and the company is operating in a challenging environment with value-conscious consumers. The initiatives are defensive rather than growth-oriented.
Carries a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) with consensus estimates showing strong growth of 10.6% in sales and 33.7% in EPS, plus a trailing four-quarter earnings surprise of 30.4%.
Holds a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) with modest sales growth of 3.7% expected, but EPS is projected to decline 2.4% year-over-year with only a 1.8% average earnings surprise.

title: 3 High-Yield Stocks Near Their 52-Week Lows That Dividend Income Investors Are Sleeping On
author: John Ballard
description: Hershey, McDonald's, and NetEase are trading near 52-week lows while offering attractive dividend yields of 3.4%, 3.1%, and 1.65% respectively—significantly higher than the S&P 500's 1% yield. Despite near-term headwinds, these industry leaders maintain strong business models and dividend growth potential, with analysts projecting solid earnings growth over the coming years.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Stock is down 11% due to high cocoa costs, but CFO indicated visibility into cocoa deflation in 2026. Strong long-term demand with 6% annual chocolate market growth expected, 20% projected earnings growth, and attractive 3.45% yield provide upside potential despite current margin pressure.

Stock down 19% YTD due to soft U.S. sales, but company just announced its 50th consecutive dividend increase with 3.1% yield. Exceptional 46.9% operating margin from franchise model, strategic initiatives, and 7.7% projected earnings growth support continued dividend increases and long-term value.

Stock down 15% this year with adjusted net income declining 8%, but decline is due to investment losses, not core business weakness. 35% operating margin, 30% five-year dividend CAGR, 40% payout ratio with room to grow, and massive China gaming market opportunity (769M players by 2030) support positive outlook.

title: Hershey (HSY) Gains As Market Dips: What You Should Know
author: Na
description: Hershey (HSY) closed at $174.34, up 1.25% despite broader market losses. The stock has declined 6.54% over the past month, underperforming the Consumer Staples sector. Analysts expect strong earnings growth of 62.31% YoY with revenue growth of 2.34%. The company holds a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) with a Forward P/E of 20.29, slightly above its industry average.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: While Hershey shows strong expected earnings growth (62.31% YoY) and positive analyst estimate revisions, the stock carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating. The stock has underperformed its sector over the past month (-6.54% vs -2.41% sector loss), and its Forward P/E ratio is slightly elevated compared to industry peers, suggesting limited upside potential in the near term despite solid fundamentals.
